messages.subject: book.rspde() function
parts:
Dear all,

I have a question concerning the usage of the book.rspde() function in INLA, found in the book "Advanced Spatial Modeling with Stochastic Partial Differential Equations Using R and INLA",  in 7.1.1 data simulation of discrete time domains. 

I draw k independent realizations of the spatial model, does that mean that I sample from the precision matrix generated from the coordinates/mesh? Why do I need the st.dev and range parameter for it too?

An answer and explanation of the function would be highly appreciated. 

Thank you very much!
Corinna

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] book.rspde() function
parts: As in the Matérn covariance, the definition of the precision matrix evaluated at the mesh nodes considering the FEM needs three parameters: smoothness, variance and the scale or range. It is described in Chapter two.
